items.title:
Build a polished responsive web application called “SIMCARD” for IdentityMD agents.

Core experience:

* The homepage must have one prominent search field that accepts an IdentityMD NFT token ID, such as 222.
* When the user presses Enter or clicks “Generate SIMCARD”, retrieve the NFT and agent’s public data and create a personalized animated SIMCARD.
* Every NFT must produce its own card using that NFT’s original artwork and dominant colors. Do not use a generic avatar.
* No wallet connection should be required to search or create a card.

Data sources:

* Use the public IdentityMD API at https://api.imd.fun and the Explorer API at https://explorer.imd.fun.
* Use GET /seats/:tokenId for the owner, agent ID, online status, attempts, accepted, rejected, failed, work, reviews and collaborators.
* Use GET /seats/:tokenId/standing for presence, dispatch eligibility and currently running jobs.
* Use GET /api/agents/:tokenId on the Explorer origin for owner name, held duration, jobs and last accepted activity.
* Use GET /seats/records to calculate rankings when possible.
* Use GET /wallets/:address/earnings to show public IMD earnings and launch allocations after resolving the NFT owner.
* Use public Ethereum NFT metadata or tokenURI for the original IdentityMD artwork.
* Reproduce the useful public information shown by Swarm Ledger, but do not scrape private information. If a data point cannot be verified from an official public API or onchain source, label it “Unavailable” rather than inventing it.

Animated SIMCARD:

* Display NFT number, original NFT artwork, verified agent status, online/offline/working state, agent ID, accepted work, total attempts, acceptance rate, runtime when publicly available, owner ENS or public handle, Ethereum network and last activity.
* Animate the original NFT artwork subtly: rotating orbital lines, pulsing center light, scanning line and live online indicator.
* The animation state must reflect real status: calm for ready, faster for working and dimmed for offline.
* Do not expose full wallet addresses by default. Show a shortened address only inside the expanded details view.
* Include a real QR code linking to the public SIMCARD profile URL for that NFT.

Interaction:

* Clicking the card must open a detailed agent profile containing payouts, allocations, work history, acceptance statistics, rank, reviews and onchain verification links whenever those fields are publicly available.
* Include links to IdentityMD Explorer, Etherscan and OpenSea.
* Provide “Download PNG” and “Download Video” buttons. Video export should create a short looping MP4 or WebM version of the animated card.
* Provide a “Share on X” button that prepares a short caption and profile link. If X cannot automatically attach the downloaded video without OAuth/API access, clearly instruct the user to attach the downloaded video manually.
* Every generated profile must have a shareable URL such as /agent/222 and social preview metadata.

Design:

* Premium minimal cyberpunk design inspired by the original IdentityMD visual language.
* Black and graphite background, neon colors derived from each NFT, crisp monospaced typography and restrained glow.
* Responsive on desktop and mobile.
* Clear loading, invalid token, missing NFT, offline API and unavailable-data states.
* Accessible controls and reduced-motion support.
* Cache public API responses briefly, but provide a Refresh button for current data.

Security and privacy:

* Read-only application.
* Never request a seed phrase, private key, token approval or transaction signature.
* Do not deploy a new token.
* Do not create financial contracts.
* Do not display VPS IP addresses, device keys, secrets or other private infrastructure data.

Deliver a complete working website connected to live public data, not a static mockup. Host the finished static frontend on IPFS and make sure all browser-side API requests work with CORS. If an official endpoint does not permit browser CORS, use an available browser-safe official endpoint or an onchain read-only fallback and document the limitation.

Deliver a complete working website connected to live public data, not a static mockup. Host the finished static frontend on IPFS and make sure all browser-side API requests work with CORS. If an official endpoint does not permit browser CORS, use an available browser-safe official endpoint or an onchain read-only fallback and document the limitation.

Improve the existing SIMCARD website. Do not rebuild it from scratch and do not remove the current animated card, token search, PNG/video download, profile links, QR code, or X sharing features.

1. Redesign the “Open profile” view

The current profile is too dark, text-heavy, and difficult to scan. Turn it into a clean dashboard made of clearly separated cards.

Use a slightly lighter charcoal background, brighter panels, clear borders, generous spacing, larger headings, and high-contrast text. Keep the current IdentityMD cyber style and each NFT’s dominant colors.

Use a two-column card grid on desktop and one column on mobile.

Display these sections as separate cards:

- Identity
- Live status
- Performance
- Rankings
- Rewards and launch allocations
- Work history
- Reviews
- Onchain verification links

Important numbers such as accepted work, acceptance rate, rank, rewards, and last activity should be visually prominent.

Do not display large paragraphs for unavailable data. Use a small muted “Unavailable” badge with a short explanation or tooltip instead.

Keep the animated SIMCARD visible at the top of the profile.

2. Fix the “Held for” calculation

The existing “Held for” value is incorrect. Calculate it from the Ethereum ERC-721 Transfer event in which the current owner most recently received this specific IdentityMD NFT.

Contract:
0x0000ec93127baa929e58e97dd0095a2bfb38ec1d

Do not use the agent pairing date, latest activity, API snapshot date, or unrelated contract activity.

Show both the readable duration and exact acquisition date, for example:

Held for: 34 days
Acquired: Aug 26, 2026

If the correct acquisition transaction cannot be verified, show “Unavailable” instead of an estimated or incorrect duration.

3. Improve live IdentityMD data handling

Retrieve the freshest available public data for the entered token ID from the official IdentityMD endpoints, including:

- /seats/:tokenId
- /seats/:tokenId/standing
- /seats/records
- /wallets/:ownerAddress/earnings
- the public Explorer agent page
- Ethereum onchain ownership, metadata, and Transfer logs

Show:

- online/offline state
- runtime
- queue
- last activity
- attempts
- accepted
- rejected
- failed
- pending
- acceptance rate
- accepted-work rank
- attempts rank
- acceptance-rate rank
- percentile
- payouts
- launch allocations
- recent work
- reviews

This remains a static IPFS frontend. If the official IdentityMD API blocks browser requests because of CORS, do not use an untrusted public CORS proxy and do not fabricate live values. Use verified onchain data plus the latest bundled snapshot, label snapshot values clearly with their timestamp, and keep a Refresh button for retrying the official API.

Structure the data-access code so a trusted first-party API proxy can be added later through one configurable base URL.

4. Improve usability

- Preserve token-ID search and direct hash routes such as #/agent/222.
- Make the profile readable without opening technical JSON.
- Place technical API and explorer links inside a compact collapsible “Verification” card.
- Add loading, invalid-token, unavailable-data, and network-error states.
- Maintain full mobile responsiveness and keyboard accessibility.
- Do not require a wallet connection.
- Do not expose private keys, API keys, or secrets.
- Ensure PNG and video exports still work after the redesign.
- Ensure the QR code and share link open the correct token profile.
- Keep the site name “SIMCARD” and the tagline “One card. Every agent. Verified onchain.”

Update the existing SIMCARD website. Preserve the current visual design, animated NFT card, routes, download buttons, QR code, X sharing, and responsive layout. This is a focused data-layer repair, not a redesign.

Replace the current failing browser API requests with the following public live IdentityMD sources:

1. Fetch `https://api.imd.fun/swarm` as the primary live source. This endpoint supports browser CORS and is cached for approximately 10 seconds. Find the requested seat by its NFT token ID and use it for live status, presence, agent ID, attempts, accepted, rejected, failed, pending, last activity, runtime and other available performance data.

2. Fetch `https://explorer.imd.fun/api/agents/{tokenId}` as a second live source. Use its available fields such as online status, owner, ownerName, held, attempts, accepted, jobs and lastAcceptedAt.

3. Use `https://api.imd.fun/seats/records` only as a fallback for statistics and rankings. Do not allow failure of this request to replace valid `/swarm` or Explorer data with “Unavailable.”

4. Calculate rankings client-side from the complete seat records when available:
   - rank by accepted work
   - rank by attempts
   - rank by acceptance rate, with the existing minimum-attempt rule
   - percentile

5. Keep Ethereum onchain reads as the authoritative source for NFT ownership, artwork and acquisition history. Calculate “Held for” from the latest ERC-721 Transfer event in which the current owner received this specific token. Do not calculate it from the site build date, snapshot date or agent pairing date.

6. Never show every field as unavailable because one endpoint failed. Merge successful results field by field. Use this priority:
   - live `/swarm` data
   - Explorer agent endpoint
   - onchain data
   - last valid snapshot
   - only then show “Unavailable” for that individual field

7. Add automatic refresh every 10 seconds for live status and statistics. Show a small “Live · updated X seconds ago” indicator. Preserve the last valid values during a temporary refresh failure.

8. Keep the Open Profile interface clean and organized in the existing card/grid layout. Do not return to a long text-heavy profile.

9. Display a small and clear data-source label for each section: “Live IMD,” “Explorer,” “Onchain,” or “Snapshot.” Do not expose technical error messages to normal users.

10. Test at least token IDs `222` and `1`. Confirm that one unavailable endpoint does not prevent the other public and onchain values from appearing.

Important: this is an IPFS-hosted static React frontend. Do not add a private backend, secret API key, wallet connection or paid API dependency. Keep the site fully read-only.

items.title:
Build SwarmWorld Core as one standalone Foundry project.

SwarmWorld is a persistent on-chain world where independent workers
submit, test, review and verify missions before world state changes.

CONTRACT

Create one Solidity contract: SwarmWorld.sol.

No token.
No owner or admin.
No upgradeability.
No pausing.
No external contracts.
Use native ETH only for mission rewards.
Deploy on Sepolia.

WORLD

Create 3 settlements with IDs 0,1,2:

0 Genesis City:
energy 500, food 500, materials 500, knowledge 500,
population 100, stability 80.

1 Iron Valley:
energy 420, food 550, materials 700, knowledge 350,
population 100, stability 75.

2 Nova Port:
energy 120, food 420, materials 300, knowledge 180,
population 100, stability 75.

energy, food, materials and knowledge are bounded 0..1000.
stability is bounded 0..100.

TIME

tick() is permissionless and may execute only once per 24 hours.

Each tick reduces energy by 25, saturating at zero, for settlements
without an active mission.

Emit Tick and EnergyCrisis when energy is below 300.

MISSIONS

The MVP supports one mission type: ENERGY_REPAIR.

Anyone may open an energy-repair mission for a settlement with
energy < 300 and no active mission.

openEnergyMission() is payable.

Reward must be > 0.

At creation specify four distinct nonzero payout addresses:
builder, tester, reviewer, verifier.

Also record four distinct uint32 IMD seat IDs for provenance.
Do not claim the contract authenticates those seat IDs.

Mission lifetime: 3 days.

Mission states:
OPEN, WORKING, VERIFYING, PASSED, FAILED, SETTLED, EXPIRED.

Only one active mission per settlement.

BUILDER

Only the builder may call submitOutcome().

Submit:
energyGain,
materialsCost,
builderArtifactHash.

Valid proposal:
energyGain 200..300 inclusive.
materialsCost <= 100.
resulting energy <= 1000.
settlement must have enough materials.

TESTER

Only tester calls submitTest(bytes32 testHash, bool pass).

If false, mission becomes FAILED.

REVIEWER

Only reviewer calls submitReview(bytes32 reviewHash, bool pass).

Reviewer must be different from builder and tester.

If false, mission becomes FAILED.

VERIFIER

Only verifier calls verifyOutcome(bytes32 verificationHash, bool pass).

If false, mission becomes FAILED.
If true after builder+tester+reviewer success, mission becomes PASSED.

SETTLEMENT

settleMission() is permissionless but only for PASSED missions.

On settlement:
add energyGain;
subtract materialsCost;
mark SETTLED;
clear the settlement active mission.

Do not modify food, knowledge, population or stability.

Compute and store a deterministic proofHash from:
missionId,
settlementId,
world-state-before hash,
energyGain,
materialsCost,
builderArtifactHash,
testHash,
reviewHash,
verificationHash,
the four seat IDs.

Emit the proofHash and world state transition.

REWARDS

Use pull payments.

Successful reward:
builder 50%
tester 15%
reviewer 15%
verifier receives the remainder (20% plus any rounding dust).

claim() must set claimable balance to zero before sending ETH.

FAILED:
mission sponsor may reclaim the full reward.

EXPIRED:
after 3 days the sponsor may expire the mission and reclaim reward.

No double settlement or double refund.

TESTS

Use Foundry.

Test at minimum:
initial world state;
exact 24h tick boundary;
energy cannot underflow;
crisis event;
one active mission per settlement;
four role addresses are distinct;
four seat IDs are distinct;
unauthorized role calls;
wrong workflow order;
energy/material bounds;
failed test;
failed review;
failed verification;
3-day expiry;
refund;
world state unchanged before settlement;
successful state transition;
deterministic proofHash;
double settlement;
double refund;
reward split;
double claim;
reentrant claim attempt.

Return source, ABI, tests, README and deployment script.

If Sepolia deployment succeeds, return contract address and tx hash.
Never fabricate deployment evidence.

Release Proof Of Work (ERC-20 symbol WORK, displayed as $WORK) on Sepolia chainId 11155111, followed by a publicly hosted, extremely simple claim website. Deploy only the fixed-supply token, protocol LP and protocol MerkleDistributor. No game, placeholder application contract, extra helper deployment or custom distributor. Use evm_project with contracts: []. The configured token-only-capable ProjectFactory supplies LP and distributor. Token contract name ProofOfWorkToken, name exactly Proof Of Work, symbol exactly WORK, 18 decimals, no constructor arguments, fixed 1 billion tokens (10^27 minor units) minted to msg.sender; no mint/admin/upgrade/tax/blacklist backdoor. Include meaningful ERC-20 tests, reproducible offline build with bytecode_hash=none, and independent review covering token and generated launch.json.
Pinned current Sepolia policy v5: 2% rewards this launch's accepted contributors by existing scoring, 8% equally among unique wallets with accepted work in preceding 12 hours, overlap combined into one leaf, 80% LP, 10% treasury, one-hour unlock. The control plane freezes allocations; workers must never invent recipients or choose economic policy. Native ETH pool, fee 3000, tickSpacing 60, policy opening fully diluted valuation 20 ETH for all 1 billion tokens = 0.00000002 ETH per WORK. Policy derives effective price; manifest initialPrice is retained for provenance but overridden by policy. Token-only liquidity, no ETH funding. No mainnet transactions.
After verified deployment, build a minimal React/Vite/TypeScript page with RainbowKit wallet connection, wagmi/viem, and no custom styling (plain browser defaults; RainbowKit's required stock CSS is fine). Title Proof Of Work, display $WORK and Sepolia. Plain text: Rewards for workers who helped build and deploy projects. Add one short explanatory sentence about the 2% launch-contributor and 8% recent-worker rewards. On connection show wallet WORK balance, allocated rewards, and currently claimable WORK. Show not eligible for absent wallet, unlock time for locked allocations, already claimed, pending, confirmed and recoverable error states. Only enable Claim when connected on Sepolia, eligible, unlocked, not claimed and deployment data is verified. Offer switch to Sepolia. After success re-read claim status and balance. No approval or transfer transaction: only distributor.claim(0,connectedWallet,allocationAmount,proof), payable to that wallet, with zero ETH value. A successful RPC read is required; failure is not zero balance or ineligibility. Test disconnected/wrong-chain, absent, locked, eligible, claimed, rejected signing, reverted transaction, and RPC failure states without broadcasting from worker keys.
Use actual .imd/reads/deployment.json for token address/chain/source/ABI and build output imd-deployment.json as mandated by workflow. The protocol distributor is not an application contract in the manifest. Discover it from GET https://api.imd.fun/launches/<handoff launchId>, artifacts role distributor. Export its address, round 0, allocation snapshot and ABI alongside site files; derive the ABI from packages/contracts/src/MerkleDistributor.sol at Identity-md platform source commit a94632d6ea40fbd2d1bcd8a0aafe53a1619956c6 in surfer77/IMD2. It uses StandardMerkleTree leaves [address,uint256] with OpenZeppelin double hashing, sorted pairs; rebuild the tree from every saved allocation wallet/amount and compare to launch.merkleRoot and on-chain roundOf(0).root. Export proofs per wallet in static claims.json, using exact decimal strings/bigints. Before enabling claim verify chain, deployed code, distributor.token() equals the handoff token, and the snapshot root equals on-chain round root; use on-chain round state for unlock/swept checks and claimed(0,wallet) for eligibility remaining. Do not add distributor to the exact attested contract set in imd-deployment.json; inventory its ABI and claims.json as additional hashed assets. No invented addresses, roots, balances or proofs. Injected wallets must work without additional operator credentials; do not invent a WalletConnect project ID.
Keep web source/package/lock/build config in web/, relative-base static export in root dist/, docs in docs/. Export implementation-derived token ABI and verify canonical ABI hash against handoff. Build, typecheck and exercise real browser interactions; publish actual evidence and state limitations. User authorizes normal configured GitHub/IPFS hosting and Sepolia deployment through existing services, not worker access to secrets or direct worker broadcasts. Finish only after source publication, verified deployment, website publication and reachability validation. All contract and workflow steps, including manifest, independent review and frontend, require the premium inference tier with approved highest-capability Claude or Codex models. No downgrade to runtime defaults or economy models.

Original request:

Repair the existing Proof Of Work claim website and republish to the SAME explicit IPFS hosting label work (work.site.identitymd.eth). Sepolia only; no new contracts or deployment. Existing launch ee1f32a2-7f0e-48f1-88c2-1c591e0bdc66. Restore the already accepted web/, dist/, docs/frontend/ from https://github.com/Identity-md/launch-109-workflow-frontend-stage-context at exact commit 1a024d2bf791b7fbc35630dc373d81146c1dde46 into your assigned workspace; preserve existing contract source. Do not rebuild the UI from scratch. The launch API was fixed to expose merkleRoot. Refresh web/data/launch.json from that API, regenerate proofs/config/snapshot and rebuild the existing site. Require the service root to equal the reconstructed StandardMerkleTree root and on-chain distributor roundOf(0).root, and require distributor.token() to match the handoff token. Missing or mismatched roots must fail the production build instead of publishing a permanently disabled claim page. Keep the plain browser-default styling and RainbowKit, wallet balance, allocation and claim states. Preserve the exact existing Sepolia deployment; only claim(0,connectedWallet,amount,proof), zero ETH, never broadcast from worker keys. Run typecheck, unit and DOM interaction tests, production build, verify:live, verify:export and check:submission. Run existing browser tests if permitted and truthfully document limitations if sandbox denies browser launch. Confirm funded round, unlock time, all 63 allocation proofs, and my wallet 0x200e710acaa6a93bbc77146026328c40f1d60fb1 allocation. Publish the accepted repaired source and validation evidence to the configured Identity-md GitHub organization, and publish the static website under existing label work. Both source publication and website hosting are explicitly required and authorized. No new token/LP/distributor. Highest approved premium model only, Claude supported.

Prior decisions:

User explicitly approved this frontend-only repair and replacing the existing work subdomain content. Token and distributor remain unchanged. API merkleRoot fix b3b266a is live.

Existing implementation objective:

Repair the accepted WORK claim page using its existing frontend source, verified existing deployment and corrected service Merkle root; test and publish the corrected static export under work.

Original request:

Build and publicly host WORK2, a clean minimal RainbowKit claim website for the existing WORK token on Sepolia. Use frontend-for-contract v5 with Vercel Web Interface Guidelines review. Choose attractive locally bundled fonts, a coherent type scale, restrained colors, generous spacing and a responsive layout. Show wallet connection, WORK balance, allocated/claimable rewards, unlock and claimed states, and concise worker-rewards copy. Format balances readably, keeping exact precision available in details.
Reuse the verified deployment ee1f32a2-7f0e-48f1-88c2-1c591e0bdc66 and corrected implementation from repair job 5592b20b-43d3-466a-84ab-15b16185201c. Fetch that job's published repository and delivery commit, import its web/, dist/, docs/frontend/ files, then improve design. Same token, distributor, round 0, allocations and claimed state: this is not a second airdrop. No new contracts, token or LP. Verify handoff, service root, reconstructed proofs and on-chain root/token before enabling claims. Retain wrong-chain, locked, ineligible, claimed and error handling; sole transaction claim(0,connectedWallet,amount,proof), zero ETH. No worker broadcasts.
Required deliverables: React/Vite/TypeScript frontend source, package/lockfile, tests, validation evidence, and a complete built relative-base static dist/ with imd-deployment.json and asset inventory. Run build, typecheck, unit/interaction tests and live read-only verification. Review current Vercel guidelines and inspect desktop/mobile in available browser tools; document actual findings, fixes and limitations.
Publish source and evidence to a public GitHub repository in the configured Identity-md organization (github:true). Publish dist/ to IPFS with exact NEW label work2 (ipfs:work2), yielding https://work2.site.identitymd.eth.limo. Preserve original work site. Both source publication and public website hosting are explicitly required and authorized. Use approved premium Claude or Codex models.

Prior decisions:

User explicitly requested pushing the design skill updates, waiting for deployment, and creating a new work2 frontend for the existing WORK contracts with minimal clean design and nice fonts. The original work site must remain available.

Existing implementation objective:

Build WORK2 as a polished minimal alternative claim frontend for the existing WORK launch, using the updated Vercel-guidelines frontend skill. Deliver the accepted source, package lockfile, tests and validation evidence to a public repository in the configured Identity-md GitHub organization (github:true), and publish dist/ through IPFS under exact label work2 (ipfs:work2). Preserve original work and all existing contracts.

Retest the complete swarm by building and launching VolatilityGuard Lab on Sepolia: VolatilityGuardHook, VolatilityGuardToken, independent adversarial review, verified factory deployment with a seeded pool, then a working public swap dapp with explanatory information. Publish real source, receipts, test evidence and the live site.

Hook: per-PoolId isolation; bounded observation ring/TWAP and EWMA volatility; adaptive price-deviation limits; rolling volume budget resistant to split swaps; NORMAL/WARMUP/GUARDED/RECOVERY states, stale/low-liquidity handling and deterministic recovery. Authenticate canonical PoolManager callbacks/accounting, never trust sender/hookData identity. Specify both swap directions and exact-input/output, units/rounding, bounded execution and caps. Keep LP exits possible and initialization/warmup non-bricking. Reverts cannot persist breaker transitions. No discretionary admin powers or claim of total MEV protection. Support arbitrary currencies.

VGL: Volatility Guard Lab, 18 decimals, no constructor args, fixed 10^27 units minted to deployer, no mint backdoor. Native ETH pair (zero address), static fee 3000, tickSpacing 60; initial sqrtPriceX96 792281625142643375935439503360000 (0.00000001 ETH/VGL). Verify Sepolia PoolManager 0xe03a1074c86cfedd5c142c4f04f1a1536e203543. Use only existing verified periphery, no new deployed helper. Workers never receive keys or broadcast deployments.

Deliver pinned/vendored Foundry project, bytecode_hash=none, offline build/test/fmt checks, fuzz/invariant/stress tests for accounting, isolation, manipulation/split volume, unauthorized callbacks, reentrancy, stale history, edge values, recovery and LP exits; report actual counts, gas, failures and limitations. Independent reviewer checks code AND launch manifest; repair blocking findings before deployment. Export ABI JSON and architecture/threat-model/integration docs with exact pool key, quote/swap/liquidity recipes and decoded errors.

After verified deployment handoff, build React/Vite/TypeScript + RainbowKit/wagmi/viem in web/, committed relative-base export in dist/. Include hook explanation, risk/limitation information and live pool dashboard (tick/TWAP, volatility, deviation, volume/state/events). Primary ETH/VGL swap UI: amounts, direction, balances/max, real quotes, slippage/minimum received, approvals and wallet-signed swaps, transaction states/errors/explorer links. Support injected wallets without extra credentials. Handle token-sided bootstrap: buy with ETH first; reverse trades depend on accrued ETH liquidity. No fabricated quotes or receipts. Add supported-position exits and clearly labeled simulation demos. Test both directions, wallet/chain states, rejected signing, guard reverts, funds/RPC errors and responsive UI. Complete only when contracts are live, source published and the functional IPFS dapp is reachable.

release.failure: Cancelled by operator. Already broadcast transactions and published artifacts cannot be undone.

Build and launch VolatilityGuard Lab as one standalone contract job on Sepolia: implement VolatilityGuardHook and VolatilityGuardToken, meaningful tests, independent adversarial review of source and launch manifest, GitHub source publication, verified factory deployment with a seeded Uniswap v4 pool. No website or IPFS deliverable.

Hook: per-PoolId isolation; bounded observation ring/TWAP and EWMA volatility; adaptive price-deviation limits; rolling volume budget resistant to split swaps; NORMAL/WARMUP/GUARDED/RECOVERY states, stale/low-liquidity handling and deterministic recovery. Authenticate canonical PoolManager callbacks/accounting, never trust sender/hookData identity. Specify both swap directions and exact-input/output, units/rounding, bounded execution and caps. Keep LP exits possible and initialization/warmup non-bricking. Reverts cannot persist breaker transitions. No discretionary admin powers or claim of total MEV protection. Support arbitrary currencies.

VGL: name Volatility Guard Lab, symbol VGL, 18 decimals, no constructor args, fixed 10^27 units minted to deployer, no mint backdoor. Native ETH pair (zero address), static fee 3000, tickSpacing 60; initial sqrtPriceX96 792281625142643375935439503360000 (0.00000001 ETH/VGL). Verify Sepolia PoolManager 0xe03a1074c86cfedd5c142c4f04f1a1536e203543. Use existing verified periphery, no new deployed helper. Workers never receive deployment keys or broadcast.

Deliver a pinned/vendored Foundry project with bytecode_hash=none, offline build/test/fmt checks, fuzz/invariant/stress tests for accounting, isolation, manipulation/split volume, unauthorized callbacks, reentrancy, stale history, edge values, recovery and LP exits. Report actual counts, gas, failures and limitations. Preserve pinned dependency contents; verify any vendor digest inventory after final formatting rather than claiming a stale check passed. Export implementation-derived ABI JSON under artifacts/abis/ and architecture/threat-model/integration documentation with exact pool-key derivation, existing quote/swap/liquidity recipes and decoded errors. Document token-sided bootstrap: buy with ETH first; reverse swaps need accrued ETH liquidity.

Resolved operator policy: Sepolia univ4_hook policy v2, never mainnet. Token/hookAdmin/treasury/LP policy owners are 0x09ec38170e94532eddb57c69dfc4f1fdcd0d4a60 without extra contract admin behavior. Supply: 80% liquidity, 10% treasury, 10% contributors; 1h contributor lock and 30% per-wallet cap. Factory seeds up to 8e26 VGL units and ZERO ETH. Deployer derives the widest aligned token-only range and affordable liquidity from the opening price using exact integer Uniswap tick math. Configured deployer gas is capped by the existing 0.3 Sepolia ETH policy; no extra funding or spending authority.

Execution boundaries: builder implements source/tests/docs/ABIs; the control plane adds a separate launch.json assignment; an independent reviewer reviews source AND canonical manifest and returns findings without changing files. Repair concrete blocking findings while preserving required behavior. Review follows supplied canonical manifest/service guidance: policy, signed artifact linkage and post-review publication/attestation are service responsibilities, not invented manifest fields. Workers submit their completed predeployment assignment without waiting for future deployment receipts or GitHub URLs. After accepted review the existing publisher creates the automatic launch repository in its configured GitHub org; verifier and deployer handle attestation, admission and deployment. The operator verifies published source and deployed contracts to assess the overall launch. DeFi references support implementation, not a separate commissioned research report.
